tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

entries.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

The third-generation Hongguang MINI EV Macaron went on sale in China on November 14, 2023. SAIC-GM-Wuling (SGMW) launched it in collaboration with SmileyWorld, and a Chinese-market report dated November 15 covered the launch. It was priced at 46,800 yuan (about 6,400 USD).

Pre-launch coverage put the date at November 15, and the reveal came earlier. The new car was expected to launch on November 15 in China. The interior images came out on November 1, 2023. Wuling Motors had unveiled the exterior design of the 3rd-generation hatchback on October 26.

Wikipedia gives an earlier, different timeline. It says a Mini EV GameBoy Edition was introduced in March 2022 and sold alongside the previous models. It is marketed as the third-generation model. So if you mean the first car marketed as "third generation," that was March 2022. If you mean the SmileyWorld Macaron, that was November 2023.

**Launch and price:** The third-generation Wuling Hongguang Mini EV Macaron entered the market on November 14, 2023, priced at 46,800 yuan (about 6,400 USD).

**Key specs (third generation):**
- **Battery:** 17.3 kWh lithium iron phosphate pack
- **Range:** 215 km (CLTC)
- **Fast charging:** 30% to 80% in 35 minutes (DC). AC charging from 20% to 100% takes five hours.
- **Airbags:** A front passenger airbag was added.
- **Screens:** An 8-inch floating central touchscreen.
- **Dimensions:** 3064/1493/1629 mm, 2010 mm wheelbase, 4.3 m minimum turning radius.
- **Other:** Rear 30 kW/92 Nm motor, 100 km/h top speed, 734 L trunk with rear seats folded, standard battery heating.

**Comparison with the previous model:** The page doesn't give figures for the previous generation, so I can't compare battery, range, charging, ESC, or screen specs. It does say the passenger airbag is new, and that the exterior and interior were both upgraded. It doesn't mention ESC at all.

# Wuling Hongguang Mini EV: Generations, Variants, and China Sales

## Generations and Variants (China Launch Dates)

| Variant | China launch | Key features from the article |
|---|---|---|
| **First generation (base)** | Retail deliveries began July 2020 | 9 to 26.5 kWh battery options; NEDC range 120–300 km |
| **Macaron (2021)** | April 2021 | Reversing camera with rear parking sonar, driver airbag, low-speed pedestrian warning; 20 kW motor |
| **GameBoy Edition (2022)** | March 2022 (marketed as third generation) | Restyled exterior; 9.2, 13.9, or 25.5 kWh battery; 20 kW or 30 kW motor |
| **Cabrio (2022)** | September 2022 | Two-door convertible based on the GameBoy body |
| **Macaron (2023)** | End of 2023 | Passenger airbag added; CLTC range 215 km; "fast charging enabling a 30% to 80% SoC charging time of 35 minutes" |
| **Second generation (fourth generation)** | Production December 2024; launched 22 February 2025 | 9.2, 13.8, 16.2, 25.1, or 26 kWh LFP battery; range 120–280 km; 3-door and 5-door hatchbacks |
| **Facelift (fifth generation)** | Unveiled February 2026 (photos released December 2025) | Revised dimensions; 3-door and 5-door versions |

**Gaps in the article:** It does not list ADAS features for any variant. Charging information appears only for the 2023 Macaron. It gives no battery or range specifics for the facelift.

**Non-China markets:** The Indonesian Aira EV (5-door, July 2026) and the Vietnamese Macaron (5-door, July 2026, 205 km and 300 km variants) are outside China.

## China Sales

| Year | Units |
|---|---|
| 2020 | 127,651 |
| 2021 | 395,451 |
| 2022 | 404,823 |
| 2023 | 237,863 |
| 2024 | 261,141 |
| 2025 | 424,983 |

The Sales section gives a different 2020 figure (119,255 units), so the article is internally inconsistent on that year.

**结论:** 宏光MINIEV四门版于2025年2月上市,CLTC续航205km,配30kW三合一电驱,支持直流快充。后来还推出了301km版和2026款第五代车型。

**2025年2月首发版本**
- **上市时间:** 有报道称上汽通用五菱于2月22日推出这款四门四座微型车,官方指导价4.48万至5.08万元。(来源:sina.cn 车圈相关文章)
- **续航:** 上汽通用五菱发布时,四门版的CLTC续航为205km,并搭载全新30kW三合一电驱。(来源:IT之家,2025年8月)
- **电池与性能:** 有试驾文章提到电池包容量为16.3kWh,0-50km/h加速4.9秒,高速时速可超过100km/h。(来源:新出行 试驾文章)
- **快充:** 直流快充为标配,官方数据是从30%充到80%约需35分钟。充电方式还包括交流慢充和家用随车充。(来源:IT之家,2025年8月)
- **尺寸:** 车身为3256×1510×1578mm,轴距2190mm,最小转弯半径4.5米。

**后续变化**
- **2025年11月:** 推出301km臻享+款,指导价5.58万元,置换补贴价5.28万元,续航提升至300公里以上。其余配置预计与205km臻享+款(5.08万元)相同。(来源:IT之家,2025年11月)
- **2026年3月:** 第五代宏光MINIEV上市,官方指导价4.48万至5.48万元,全系为四门四座。直流快充依然是标配,301km版的快充时间据报道为30%至80%最快35分钟。(来源:sina.cn 2026年8月文章)

如果你问的是2025年2月那一款,参考的是205km版本的数据。若要购买,建议以当地经销商和官方最新公告为准,因为价格和补贴经常调整。

I couldn't find a CnEVPost article in these results, so the details below come from CarNewsChina, Gasgoo (via metal.com), Autohome, and Wikipedia. Those sources agree on the core facts.

**Launch:** GAC's Aion brand launched the S Max on October 26, 2023. A pre-launch CarNewsChina article said the new car was previously declared by the Chinese MIIT and is expected to launch on October 26 in China with a starting price of less than 150,000 yuan. A Gasgoo-sourced report later confirmed that the AION S MAX officially hit the market on October 26, 2023 as a compact sedan.

**Replacing the S Plus:** CarNewsChina's launch coverage says the Aion S Max sedan has replaced the Aion S Plus. It also describes the S Max as a facelift of the S Plus. Wikipedia is less explicit, saying only that another new variant, the Aion S Max, went on sale in 2023.

**Changes from the S Plus:**
- **Size:** It is 53 mm longer and 10 mm wider than its predecessor. Its wheelbase is also 10 mm longer.
- **Styling:** Its front end adopted split headlights with four LED strips. CarNewsChina also notes that the exterior styling of the Aion S Max is too clean. As a result, it is hard to distinguish it from other China-made EV sedans.

## Aion V Versions and China Launches

**1. First generation Aion V (2020)**
- **China launch:** Revealed on GAC New Energy's WeChat account on 14 May 2020, with launch set for 16 June 2020.
- **Key features:**
  - Four trims were named in the article: V 60, V 70, and V 80 Max, with NEDC ranges of 400 km, 530 km, and 600 km.
  - A 135 kW permanent-magnet synchronous motor and a CATL lithium-ion battery.
  - Huawei 5G and V2X communication systems.
  - Customizable color options, including a two-tone paint option.

**2. Aion V Plus (2021 refresh)**
- **China launch:** Unveiled in September 2021, with the rapid-charging version officially launched in late September 2021.
- **Key features:**
  - Redesigned front and rear styling and interior, with a 15.6-inch infotainment display.
  - Three battery sizes (70–95 kWh), two motors, and total output of 163–200 kW.
  - NEDC range of 500–702 km.
  - SPEED+ battery (72.3 kWh): 30% to 80% in about 10 minutes, with 0–80% in 16 minutes.
  - SPEED++ battery was announced but had not reached the market as of the article's information.
  - Charging of up to 880 V and 480 kW, though only one 480 kW station existed in Guangzhou as of October 2021.
  - Battery rated to keep 95% capacity after 1,600 cycles.

**3. Second generation Aion V (2024)**
- **China launch:** Debuted at the 2024 Beijing Auto Show, with Chinese sales starting in July 2024. In China it is marketed as the Aion V 霸王龙 (Bàwáng lóng).
- **Key features:**
  - Built on GAC's AEP 3.0 electric platform, with a fully liquid-cooled electric drive.
  - An AI cockpit using the ADiGO Sense model and the ADiGO Pilot driver-assistance system, powered by an Nvidia Orin X chip and lidar.
  - Battery options of 62 kWh and 75 kWh (LFP) and 90 kWh (NMC).
  - Power output of 100–165 kW and CLTC range of 520–750 km.
  - Shorter wheelbase (2,775 mm) than the first generation.
  - A 2025 facelift was later released.
  - The related Aion i60 (EREV/BEV variant) launched in 2025.

The 2025 款 AION Y Plus launched in June 2025, not 2024. Sources also disagree on the year, so I'd check the date before relying on it.

**Launch and pricing**
- The 2025 model launched on June 3. 新车共提供 4 款车型，售价 9.98-12.38 万元, which is about 99,800 to 123,800 yuan across four versions.

Owners of older cars can also use the PAD interface and phone-car connection. A later OTA update added 车机升级增加超百款App and CarLink/HiCar support.
- **Dimensions:** These stayed the same as the 2023 model, at 4535/1870/1650 mm with a 2750 mm wheelbase.

**Launch timeline (China)**

- **EMPOW55 Concept:** Previewed in 2020 at the Guangzhou Auto Show in semi-concept form.
- **Production Empow (1.5T, 270T):** Officially launched at the 2021 Shanghai Auto Show, with sales starting in 2021.
- **Hybrid:** Introduced in late 2022.
- **Empow R 400T (2.0T):** Introduced at the 2023 Shanghai Auto Show and available from April 2023.
- **Empow R × ABT:** Also shown at the 2023 Shanghai Auto Show, with sales slated to start by the end of 2023.
- **Facelifts:** The article does not describe a facelift of the Empow itself. It mentions only a facelift of the predecessor GA4 in early 2021.
- **R-Style:** The article doesn't mention an "R-Style" version. The closest match is the Empow R.

**China yearly sales**

| Year | Units |
|------|-------|
| 2023 | 41,065 |
| 2024 | 23,707 |
| 2025 | 11,333 |
| 2026 | 1,423 |

The article gives no figures for 2021 or 2022. The 2026 figure was retrieved on 2026-02-09, so it may be a partial-year total.

**Note:** The page has no information on a 2023 facelift of the second-generation GS4 or the GS4 Plus. The only facelifts it covers are the first-generation GS4 (June 2018) and a September 2018 update for the PHEV's 2019 model year.

**GS4 Max (fourth generation per the section heading)**
- **Launch:** Trumpchi announced it in March 2024, and it is listed as in production from 2024. It is a redesigned version of the Trumpchi Emkoo and replaces the second-generation GS4 and the GS4 Plus.
- **Engine and transmission:** 1.5 L turbocharged I4 (4A15J2) with a 7-speed dual-clutch transmission, producing 130 kW (177 PS) and 270 N·m.
- **Efficiency and range:** Trumpchi claims 6.8 L/100 km (WLTC) and about 800 km of range.
- **Performance:** Official 0–100 km/h time of 8.8 s and a top speed of 190 km/h.
- **Dimensions:** 2,750 mm wheelbase, 4,685 mm length, 1,901 mm width, 1,690 mm height, and 1,540 kg curb weight.

The article is inconsistent about the generation number. The introduction calls the GS4 Max the "third generation," while its section heading and infobox call it the fourth. The fifth-generation section also refers to the 2026 model as the "fourth generation."

The article doesn't cover a "2022 Grand Master" edition or specific 2024/2025 China updates. It does describe the following:

**First generation (GM8, 2017–2022)**
- **Launch:** Debuted at the 2017 Auto Guangzhou as Trumpchi's first MPV. It was "launched in the Chinese car market in the first quarter of 2018."

**Second generation (2022–present)**
- **Launch:** Debuted at the 2022 Chengdu Auto Show with petrol, mild hybrid (HEV), and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) versions.
- **Powertrains:** The petrol engine is a new 2.0-litre turbo rated at 251 hp and 380 N⋅m. The hybrid uses a 190 hp 2.0-litre turbo with a fourth-generation THS II-based Toyota hybrid system. Gearboxes are a CVT or an 8-speed automatic.
- **Interior:** A 12.3-inch driver display, a 14.6-inch suspended central screen, and a three-spoke steering wheel.

**E9 PHEV (2023)**
- The plug-in hybrid variant of the second generation, launched in 2023.
- Combined output is 367 hp and 630 N⋅m, with a 0–100 km/h time of 8.8 seconds.
- It uses a two-speed dedicated hybrid transmission and also has a Master Edition.

**New features:**
- **Exterior:** A refreshed grille, redesigned lower bumper, new wheel designs, and two new paint colors (yellow and grey).
- **Rear:** A button to open the trunk.
- **Interior:** Twin 12.3-inch screens (unchanged), plus new infotainment options such as custom wallpapers and Amap navigation.
- **Battery and climate:** Automatic protection for the small 12V battery, and a heat pump air conditioner for better efficiency.
- **Controls and seats:** Upgraded steering-wheel touch buttons with more soft materials, and sportier seat patterns.
- **Powertrain:** A permanent-magnet synchronous motor rated at 120 kW and 240 N·m, with NEDC range of 416 km or 501 km depending on the version.

以下是我查到的奕炫改款和新增车型信息。注意:我去掉了查询中的 "OR" 运算符,直接搜索了关键词。

**2023年**
- 新款奕炫冠军版在2023年6月2日上市,官方指导价8.99-9.39万元,共推出2个型号车款。作为改款车型,外观造型更为动感,内饰设计也更加精致舒适。
- 奕炫GS马赫版在2023年3月26日上市,共推出3款配置车型,售价区间为8.59-9.99万元。
- 奕炫MAX超幻潮爸版在2023年2月上市,售价10.79万元,作为新增车型,在配置方面有所调整(原文较长,具体配置请点开原文查看)。

**2024年**

- 2024款奕炫MAX于8月21日焕新上市,官方指导价9.79万-11.99万元。外观方面,音爆数字格栅进行了扁平化升级;配置方面,新增了疾风运动套件,包括全包围和运动尾翼;内饰则新增深蓝色与浅米色的搭配。

- **Comfort:** The six-seat Dual Hybrid offers an "Executive Luxury" package with driver and front-passenger massage, heated second-row seats, four-way lumbar support, and a front-passenger "boss button."
- **Styling:** A more exaggerated front grille, black cladding, a floating-roof look from blacked-out B-C-D pillars, and vertically styled taillights.

**Unchanged:** Dimensions are expected to stay at 5015/1950/1780 mm with a 2920 mm wheelbase. Powertrains carry over: a 2.0T gasoline engine (252 hp, 400 Nm) and a hybrid with 372 hp combined output.

**Second generation (2021 onward)**

- **Launch:** The page says the second-generation GS8 was "unveiled in July 2021," with a "longer, wider body and a longer wheelbase" than the first generation.

- **Gasoline:** A 2.0 L turbo four-cylinder with an 8-speed automatic, rated at 185 kW (252 PS) and 400 N·m.
- **Hybrid (GS8 Hybrid, 2021):** Uses a Toyota-sourced hybrid system with a CVT, rated at 174 kW (237 PS).
- **Plug-in hybrid (ES9, 2023):** A 2.0 L turbo engine with a single electric motor and a 2-speed DHT, rated at 274 kW (373 PS) and 630 N·m. It has a 25.57 kWh battery and a claimed 110 km WLTC electric range.

- **Hongqi:** H5 2nd gen 2022-07-26, HS5 facelift 2023-05-21, 2025 H5 2024-09-21.
- **Roewe:** RX5 3rd gen 2022-08-05, i5 facelift 2023-07-12.
- **Voyah:** Dreamer facelift 2024-09-19.
- **Beijing:** X7 facelift 2023-04-16, EU5 PLUS 2023-08.

Doubts:
1. **Rough or estimated baseline sales:**
   - Beijing EU5 PLUS (~30k) and Beijing X7 (~40k) are guesses. I found no clean 2022 per-model figures, so these two rows may fail the 20k cut.
   - GS4 (~95k) is extrapolated from 73k through September 2022.
   - Empow Hybrid (~36k) is back-calculated from 2022 sales of 45,439, up 25%.
   - Xingchen (~50k) is estimated from more than 25k in its first two months after the September 2021 launch.
2. **Borderline rows:**
   - Voyah Dreamer's baseline is 20,683 (2023), just over the cut.
   - The 2025 Hongqi H5 claims a "new" 1.5T HEV, but a 1.5T HEV already existed in 2022.
   - The Empow R 2.0T has only month precision (2023-04), and the 2.0T may count as a trim rather than a version.
   - The GS4 2023 row's only verified new feature is the new engine.
   - The GameBoy may be a body variant rather than a version of the Mini EV.
3. **Imprecise previous_launch dates:**
   - Some are year-only: Aion S Plus "2021", Aion Y "2021", HS5 "2019", H5 1st gen "2018", X7 "2020", GS4 "2021".
   - Dreamer's original launch "2022-05" conflicts with Wikipedia, which says March 2022.
4. **Left out on purpose:**
   - Below about 20k baseline: Voyah Free, Hongqi H9 2024 facelift, IM models, Hyptec, Aion V/Free earlier updates.
   - Baseline unknown: Baojun KiWi EV DJI version (2022-09-15) and Hongqi E-QM5 update (2022-08-17).
   - Little or no new equipment: Aion S Plus/Y Plus 2023 refresh.
   - Launched after 2025-03: MG5 2026 MY, Aion Y Plus 2025 MY, Voyah Free 2nd gen.
   - Separate nameplate in China tables: GS4 MAX (Wikipedia calls it a later GS4 generation).
   - GS8 2nd gen launched 2021-12, before the window.
   - Dongfeng Aeolus/Forthing updates looked like trim editions only.
   - I found no qualifying JAC/Yiwei or MG China transitions, though that search was incomplete.

A follow-up run with fresh search budget should check Dongfeng (Aeolus, Forthing, eπ), BAIC (BJ40, U5 PLUS) and the BAIC baselines.
